summary:
Both claims are CONFIRMED. Reused the same-day ledger evidence and reopened the official sources; actionability was assessed independently. Both timestamps represent 2026-10-01T00:00:01Z. No material change is required. This verifies documented semantics, not local implementation behavior.

Landscape scan covered all five topics for 2026-08-11 through 2026-10-10. Five findings:
1. Generative video evaluation: [VGI-Bench: Probing Visual Intelligence in Video Generation Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19583v3), v3 dated 2026-08-26; accessed 2026-10-10. The authors emphasize evaluating the evolving process as well as the final state. Relevance: useful context for video-evaluation design; no change to this datetime step.
2. Human evaluation protocols: [PANEL: An Open-Source, Self-Hosted Web Platform for Human Evaluation of Generative Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31392v1), dated 2026-09-25; accessed 2026-10-10. Describes controlled multimodal studies, exportable study specifications and pilot-based power analysis. Relevance: human-study reproducibility; no change to this step.
3. Judge reliability and selective evaluation: [JEV-as-a-Judge: Accept When Confident, Escalate When Unsure](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26550v4), dated 2026-10-06; accessed 2026-10-10. Studies confidence-based escalation with thresholds fixed before testing, while reporting weaker routing on adversarial style and reference-free prose. Relevance: selective judges require local validation; this does not affect Python comparison semantics.
4. Intent/context-conditioned evaluation: [From Evaluation to Enhancement: Benchmarking and Improving Think-with-Video Reasoning for Video Generative Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11242v1), dated 2026-09-10; accessed 2026-10-10. Its evaluation separates visual fluency, task-rule adherence and goal realization. Relevance: supports distinguishing presentation quality from intended-task success; no change to this step.
5. Provenance and annotation standards: [IBC paper on provenance in media workflows released](https://iptc.org/news/ibc-paper-on-provenance-in-media-workflows-released/), dated 2026-09-28; accessed 2026-10-10. IPTC describes a C2PA implementation framework addressing editorial decisions, metadata-loss vulnerabilities and signing responsibilities. This is workflow guidance, not a new normative standard. Relevance: provenance workflow design only; no change to this step. No relevant annotation-standard revision within the scan window was verified.

No proposals: these landscape findings do not establish a material addition to the supplied step.
